CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VD

PUBLIC AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25 (1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by: a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence; b. providing protection to victims;
c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence; d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children; e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;
f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or g. disseminating information about laws and regulations related to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26 (1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

Sufficiently clear Article 8 Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by "complaint service" is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.

Letter b What is meant by "health service" is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by "spiritual guidance" is a form of activity in which there is a process of spiritual guidance and coaching for humans so that it can provide peace, tranquility and coolness of heart to humans by always providing encouragement and motivation to remain patient, trust in God and continue to carry out their obligations.

Letter f What is meant by "social rehabilitation service" is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

Letter g What is meant by "legal aid and assistance service" is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

Letter h Sufficiently clear Letter i What is meant by "repatriation and reintegration" is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 29 Financing for the protection of women and children from acts of violence may be sourced from: a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other lawful sources that are non-binding in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 30 (1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that carry out protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VID

INFORMATION AND REPORTING SYSTEM Article 27 (1) The Regional Government prepares and compiles an information and reporting system for the protection of women and children from acts of violence. (2) The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 31 Activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence organized by P2TP2A before this Regional Regulation is promulgated, are declared to remain valid until the establishment of the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Child Protection Service by the Regional Government.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CHILD PROTECTION

Protection of Child Victims of Acts of Violence

Part Four

Empowerment of Victims of Acts of Violence

Article 13

1. The Regional Government shall empower victims of acts of violence in the form of: a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and c. capital assistance.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.

5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VD

PUBLIC AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25 (1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by: a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence; b. providing protection to victims;
c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence; d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children; e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;
f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or g. disseminating information about laws and regulations related to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26 (1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VD

PUBLIC AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25 (1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by: a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence; b. providing protection to victims;
c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence; d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children; e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;
f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or g. disseminating information about laws and regulations related to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26 (1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

Article 13

1. The Regional Government shall empower victims of acts of violence in the form of: a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and c. capital assistance.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

BAB V

INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN EMPOWERMENT

Article 20 (1) In the context of services for victims of violence, the Regional Government shall establish P2TP2A.

2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 30 (1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that carry out protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VD

PUBLIC AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25 (1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by: a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence; b. providing protection to victims;
c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence; d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children; e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;
f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or g. disseminating information about laws and regulations related to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26 (1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.

25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 29 Financing for the protection of women and children from acts of violence may be sourced from: a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other lawful sources that are non-binding in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 30 (1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that carry out protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VID

INFORMATION AND REPORTING SYSTEM Article 27 (1) The Regional Government prepares and compiles an information and reporting system for the protection of women and children from acts of violence. (2) The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 31 Activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence organized by P2TP2A before this Regional Regulation is promulgated, are declared to remain valid until the establishment of the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Child Protection Service by the Regional Government.

NUMBER YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;

19. ::

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CHAPTER VD

PUBLIC AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25 (1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by: a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence; b. providing protection to victims;
c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence; d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children; e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;
f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or g. disseminating information about laws and regulations related to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26 (1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

b. other lawful sources that are non-binding in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred;
13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, counseling techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

::

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the administration of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
